scope: All 100 prompts, four answers and rationales individually read; primary references inspected; semantic overlap search of canonical bank. Draft unchanged; apply recommendedChanges before acceptance.
sourceAccessNote: Direct page opens and primary indexed pages used. Cambridge often returned 403 on direct opens, so its indexed editorial definitions were read. Provisional URLs that failed or lacked the exact claim have explicit replacements. No source wording copied into questions.

rows.prompt: Which legume forms the base of a classic hummus?
rows.note: Classic hummus is chickpea-based; the qualifier excludes modern pea and bean variants.

rows.prompt: Which fruit is the main ingredient in guacamole?
rows.note: Avocado is the defining guacamole base; the other fruits do not fit.

rows.prompt: Tahini is a paste made by grinding which seeds?
rows.note: Tahini is sesame paste; all three alternative seeds are distinct.

rows.prompt: Which vegetable is grated or finely chopped into a classic tzatziki?
rows.note: Cucumber, rather than the three root vegetables, is the classic tzatziki addition.

rows.prompt: Which herb gives classic pesto alla genovese its green colour?
rows.note: The Genovese qualifier identifies basil rather than other green pesto variants.

rows.prompt: Which nuts are traditionally used in pesto alla genovese?
rows.note: Traditional Genovese pesto uses pine nuts; named alternatives are substitutions.

rows.prompt: Which ingredient is whisked with oil to make a traditional mayonnaise?
rows.note: Egg yolk supplies the traditional mayonnaise emulsion; no competing listed emulsifier fits.

rows.prompt: What is the main dairy ingredient in a traditional béchamel sauce?
rows.note: Milk supplies the liquid dairy base of bechamel; cream and cheese are not that base.

rows.prompt: Which two ingredients form the basic liquid mixture in a vinaigrette?
rows.note: Oil and vinegar uniquely form a classic vinaigrette; replace the inaccessible recipe URL.

rows.prompt: What does tomato purée usually refer to in British cooking?
rows.note: British tomato puree is concentrated paste; replace the provisional URL with a producer reference.

rows.prompt: Couscous is traditionally made from which cereal grain?
rows.note: Traditional couscous is durum-wheat semolina; none of the other cereals fits.

rows.prompt: Polenta is commonly made from ground what?
rows.note: The common modern form is maize meal; commonly avoids excluding older non-maize preparations.

rows.prompt: Which type of rice is commonly used for risotto?
rows.note: Arborio is the conventional risotto rice among these choices; source explicitly confirms its starch.

rows.prompt: What shape is spaghetti?
rows.note: Spaghetti is long thin strands; use the pasta manufacturer page that explicitly describes shape.

rows.prompt: Which pasta name is associated with bow-tie shapes?
rows.note: Farfalle is bow-tie pasta; replace the inaccessible collection URL with the manufacturer.

rows.prompt: Lasagne is usually assembled using which pasta shape?
rows.note: Lasagne sheets support the layered construction; the recipe explicitly instructs layering sheets.

rows.prompt: What does al dente describe when cooking pasta?
rows.note: Al dente is firmness to the bite; correct but replace implausible temperature/medium distractors.

answers: Soft enough to squash without chewing
Crisp and browned on the outside

rows.prompt: Bulgur is made from which grain?
rows.note: Bulgur is processed wheat; the replacement cookery guide explicitly distinguishes it from raw cracked wheat.

rows.prompt: Which of these is a pulse rather than a cereal grain?
rows.note: Lentils are pulses while the other choices are cereal grains; original FAO URL returns 404.

rows.prompt: Which cereal is traditionally the main ingredient in British flapjacks?
rows.note: British flapjacks use oats; the geographic qualifier correctly excludes US pancakes.

rows.prompt: What does simmering mean?
rows.note: Simmering uses gently bubbling liquid; the other methods do not fit.

rows.prompt: Which method cooks food in hot vapour rather than submerging it in water?
rows.note: Steaming surrounds food with vapour; use the technique page, which explicitly covers it.

rows.prompt: What happens to food when it is deep-fried?
rows.note: Deep frying immerses food in fat; shallow frying is correctly excluded.

rows.prompt: What does it mean to dice a vegetable?
rows.note: Dicing makes cubes, though culinary dice can be small, medium or large; remove unnecessary size restriction.

rows.prompt: When a recipe asks you to grate cheese, what should you produce?
rows.note: Grating cheese produces small shreds; the other shapes and states are different operations.

rows.prompt: What does basting a roast involve?
rows.note: Basting applies cooking liquid or fat during roasting; use a direct definition instead of an example-only PDF.

rows.prompt: What is a food purée?
rows.note: Puree describes a smooth crushed mixture; neither strips nor whole food qualifies.

rows.prompt: What does reducing a sauce do?
rows.note: Reduction concentrates a sauce by evaporation; replace the broad PDF with a practical reduction reference.

rows.prompt: What does deglazing a frying pan involve?
rows.note: Deglazing releases browned residues into liquid; pan seasoning, flouring and washing are different.

rows.prompt: A recipe says to preheat the oven. What does that mean?
rows.note: Preheating happens before food is added; Cambridge indexed definition explicitly confirms this.

rows.prompt: What does kneading help develop in a wheat bread dough?
rows.note: Kneading develops a wheat dough gluten network; the other proposed effects are different processes.

rows.prompt: Which gas produced by yeast helps bread dough rise?
rows.note: Yeast fermentation produces carbon dioxide; the other listed gases do not raise bread by fermentation.

rows.prompt: What does proofing bread dough mean?
rows.note: Proofing means letting bread dough rise; freezing, slicing and icing do not fit.

rows.prompt: What is a sourdough starter?
rows.note: A starter is a live fermenting culture; the alternatives are not cultures.

rows.prompt: Why are cuts often made on the top of bread dough just before baking?
rows.note: Scoring guides expansion; it cannot replace fermentation or mix ingredients.

rows.prompt: What is the main reason for gently folding whipped egg whites into a cake mixture?
rows.note: Folding preserves the egg-white foam; replace inaccessible URL with explicit expert discussion.

rows.prompt: In baking, what does creaming butter and sugar mean?
rows.note: Creaming aerates softened butter and sugar; the definition and grammar are clear.

rows.prompt: What is an egg wash commonly brushed onto pastry for?
rows.note: Egg wash promotes a shiny browned pastry surface; replace inaccessible URL with baking-science coverage.

rows.prompt: Which ingredient is normally included in self-raising flour but not plain flour?
rows.note: Self-raising flour contains a raising agent; use the verified flour glossary.

rows.prompt: What does blind baking a pastry case mean?
rows.note: Blind baking cooks the pastry case before filling; replace 404 and remove joke distractor.

answers: Baking it before adding the filling
Baking it together with a raw filling
Cooking the filling separately in a saucepan
Baking it under a second layer of pastry

rows.prompt: Which citrus fruit is typically yellow when ripe and known for its sour juice?
rows.note: Lime is also yellow when fully ripe, so the original has two defensible answers; replace lime with orange.

recommendedChanges.rationale: Lemons are characteristically yellow and sour; the other listed citrus fruits normally ripen orange. Lime was excluded because ripe limes can also be yellow.

rows.prompt: What is the fragrant coloured outer layer of citrus peel called in cooking?
rows.note: Zest is the coloured exterior, distinct from the white pith and internal pulp; replace 404 URL.

rows.prompt: What is an individual segment of a garlic bulb called?
rows.note: An individual garlic-bulb division is a clove; the other botanical terms do not fit.

rows.prompt: Which vegetable is known as zucchini in American English?
rows.note: Zucchini and courgette are regional names for the same vegetable; the glossary confirms both.

rows.prompt: Which vegetable is traditionally used for sauerkraut?
rows.note: Sauerkraut uses fermented cabbage; the original recipe URL returns 404.

rows.prompt: Which herb has feathery leaves and is often paired with salmon?
rows.note: Dill matches both feathery foliage and the fish pairing; source replacement needed.

rows.prompt: Which herb has stiff, narrow leaves resembling small needles?
rows.note: Rosemary has needle-like leaves; the other listed herbs do not.

rows.prompt: Which spice is made from the bark of a tree?
rows.note: Cinnamon is bark; cumin/coriander are seed spices and pepper is fruit.

rows.prompt: Paprika is made by drying and grinding which ingredient?
rows.note: Paprika is dried ground Capsicum peppers; the three other vegetables are not its base.

rows.prompt: Which ingredient gives many curries a strong yellow colour?
rows.note: Turmeric provides yellow pigment; the dark alternative spices do not.

rows.prompt: What is the principal ingredient in a plain omelette?
rows.note: A plain omelette is based on eggs; potatoes and flour are not its principal ingredient.

rows.prompt: Which dish is a baked pastry case with a savoury egg-and-cream filling?
rows.note: Quiche uniquely combines a pastry case with savoury egg custard.

rows.prompt: Which meat is traditionally used in shepherd’s pie?
rows.note: Lamb is traditional shepherds pie meat, whereas beef identifies cottage pie.

rows.prompt: What topping is traditionally used on a shepherd’s pie?
rows.note: Mashed potato is the traditional topping; puff pastry would describe a different pie.

rows.prompt: What is the main grain in a traditional paella?
rows.note: Paella is a rice dish; variation in proteins does not affect the answer.

rows.prompt: What gives sushi rice its characteristic tangy seasoning?
rows.note: Vinegar seasons sushi rice; replace the general MAFF index with a specific recipe.

rows.prompt: Sashimi is typically served as slices of what?
rows.note: Typical fish sashimi is raw sliced fish; typically avoids claiming all sashimi must be fish.

rows.prompt: What is distinctive about tempura?
rows.note: Tempura is batter-fried food; replace the inaccessible URL and unrealistic distractors.

answers: Ingredients are coated in light batter and fried
Ingredients are simmered slowly in broth
Ingredients are baked inside a pastry crust
Ingredients are rolled in vinegared rice

rows.prompt: Which flatbread is traditionally used to wrap a burrito?
rows.note: A tortilla is the burrito wrapper; the other breads cannot describe the traditional wrap.

rows.prompt: Falafel is commonly made from which type of ingredient?
rows.note: Falafel can use chickpeas or broad beans; the grouped correct choice preserves both regional traditions.

rows.prompt: What process turns cream into butter?
rows.note: Churning separates butterfat from cream; the other preservation processes do not.

rows.prompt: Which liquid is left over when traditional butter is churned?
rows.note: Traditional buttermilk is the leftover churning liquid; wording excludes modern cultured substitutes.

rows.prompt: Which ingredient is the base of traditional dairy yogurt?
rows.note: Dairy yogurt is fermented milk; dairy qualifier excludes plant alternatives.

rows.prompt: What gives blue cheeses their coloured veins?
rows.note: Blue veins are mould cultures; replace inaccessible source and distracting non-food slate option.

recommendedChanges.rationale: Blue cheese veins are mould growth, not caramelisation, fruit pigment or salt crystals.

rows.prompt: What is the yellow central part of a hen’s egg called?
rows.note: Yolk names the central yellow portion; albumen, shell and membrane are different parts.

rows.prompt: Which part of an egg is mainly used to make a traditional meringue?
rows.note: Traditional meringue uses egg white; the other egg parts do not form its base.

rows.prompt: What makes scrambled eggs different from a plain fried egg?
rows.note: Scrambling mixes eggs as they set; replace fanciful distractors with actual alternative egg methods.

answers: The eggs are beaten and stirred as they cook
The eggs are boiled whole in their shells
The eggs are cracked into simmering water
The eggs are fried with the yolks left intact

rows.prompt: In a soft-boiled egg, how is the yolk usually served?
rows.note: Soft boiling leaves a runny or softly set yolk; replace 404 and implausible distractors.

answers: Firm and crumbly all the way through
Separated and cooked in a frying pan

rows.note: Burrata encloses a creamy filling in mozzarella; other cheeses are solid aged cheeses.

Toast it evenly in a pan

rows.prompt: What is a garnish?
rows.note: Garnish describes a finishing food decoration/accompaniment; the other choices are equipment.

rows.prompt: Which taste is associated with lemon juice?
rows.note: Independent follow-up review by botany_author: replace repeated sour-lemon fact with the savoury taste name. NIDCD explicitly gives broth, meat extracts and some cheeses as examples. Existing bank asks for glutamate, rather than naming this taste from foods.

recommendedChanges.prompt: What is the name of the savoury basic taste associated with foods such as meat broth and aged cheese?
recommendedChanges.rationale: Umami names the savoury basic taste; broth and some cheeses supply glutamate, while sour, sweet and bitter are separate taste qualities.

rows.prompt: Which basic taste is particularly associated with strong, unsweetened coffee?
rows.note: Unsweetened coffee commonly tastes bitter; sour is deliberately not a distractor; direct taste definition gives coffee as its example.

rows.prompt: Which basic taste is associated with salt?
rows.note: Salt tasting salty is tautological; replace this row with a simple nonduplicate ketchup ingredient question.

recommendedChanges.prompt: Which ingredient is the main base of the familiar red ketchup served with chips?
recommendedChanges.rationale: The familiar red ketchup is tomato-based; the other red vegetables do not form its conventional base.

rows.prompt: What does tbsp usually stand for in a recipe?
rows.note: Tbsp means tablespoon; tsp denotes teaspoon, and the other expansions are not recipe abbreviations.
